correctness.rationale: An induced P3 in a rook graph equals three corners of a 2x2 rectangle, and selected edges of K_mn form a disjoint star forest exactly when their line graph is cluster. The maximality trichotomy follows from uncovered shores, and the associated Stirling formula counts uniquely oriented nontrivial stars plus unoriented isolated edges. The rectangular spectrum is proved by star-component bounds and explicit realizations. The independent finite checker enumerates 1,152,910 subsets with exact agreement.

value.rationale: Cluster deletion is a natural hereditary induced-subgraph problem. The theorem gives a nontrivial complete labeled size distribution in a two-parameter family, separates spanning and one-sided exceptional maximal sets, and proves a sharp cardinality spectrum with n-m-1 consecutive absent sizes when n>=2m>=4. These are not consequences of the known decision dichotomy or broad forest count.
